notes.content:
Howdy, friends!

We are thrilled to wheel out to you two big beats today - the release of the highly anticipated Patch 1.1 for Moonshine Inc. and the Klabater Publisher Sale kick-off!

Today's update is not only about fine-tuning your clandestine operations and taking your moonshining mastery to new heights but also about enriching your game collection. Prepare yourselves for a wave of improvements and new titles that will truly transform your gaming experience.

PATCH 1.1

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/defd32d023c2292b68ea8d8d777c5ad2b91779ac.jpg

We've squashed many pesky bugs and we want to make sure every step of your moonshining journey is as smooth as that delicious aged bourbon. 

But the most important update is here. Brace yourselves for an array of thrilling new features and rebalancing tweaks - we've meticulously fine-tuned the mechanics, ensuring a more dynamic and immersive journey as you craft the finest moonshine. We’ve managed to secure a lot of desired rebalancing in each step of creating the moonshine - starting from general updates, to fermentation, distillation, and bottling.

Your stills will hum with newfound precision, giving you that extra edge you've been craving. Check out the patch notes: 

FIxes:


 Removed bugs in the tutorial that were blocking progress.
 Swapped Durability and Cleanliness bars in both the workshop and 3D Map, as they were incorrectly placed.
 Adjusted the "Helpful" achievement so it will no longer unlock if a player fails a mission.
 Optimized tutorial hitboxes for better performance.

New features:

1. General:

 Stash Alert has been upgraded to increase levels based on the duration moonshine is in the stash, not only the volume sold.
 The fermentation panel now features a new, more transparent, user interface.
 Batch Quality calculation has been updated and rebalanced.
 All recipes now require a fixed flavor match of 90% to begin production. However, new technologies can decrease this threshold by 5%.
 Russian language support has been added


2. Fermentation:

 Rebalanced the number of hidden flavors each yeast provides
 The generation of flavors on the timeline has changed to provide a more predictable output when fermentation parameters are tweaked.
 Flavor creation will consistently occur during the fermentation process. However, the concentration of these flavors will now vary based on the choices made and the specific settings adjusted during fermentation.


3. Distillation:

 To enhance clarity and consistency between input and output volumes during the distillation process, we've added a water jar at the end. This jar collects the residual water from distillation, which should not be included in the final product. Previously, this element of the process was not transparent, leading to potential misunderstandings and inaccurate volume calculations. Now, players can better understand and control the quality of their final product.


4. Bottling: 

 We've updated the impact of fortification/dilution on the batch flavor profile. Now, these actions will significantly affect the flavor of the batch. This means that adding water will noticeably affect the flavor match, preventing the creation of overly diluted or fortified products.

Sandbox Mode, Feb 23rd

Depending on the base chosen to start with, all deliveries will start from there. All stashes will be open from the get-go.

Additionally, the Sandbox will give options effects:

 Starting Base 
The base the player choses to start with defines which base and store are going to be used on the map, and which environment the player going to have in their base. 

 Buildings start at max level 
If checked, the player will start with all their buildings (Headquarters, Garage, Workshop) already at level 3, which it the highest one. 

 Instant Deliveries 
If checked, when the player starts a delivery, it’ll be done instantly. 

 All techs unlocked 
If checked, the player will already have all technologies unlocked from the beginning. 

 Unlimited Money 
If checked, player will have unlimited money.  

 Instant Craft, Fermentation, Distillation 
If checked, all crafts, fermentation and distillations become instantaneous. They still all require to have workers. 

 Speed Multiplier for Craft, Fermentation, Distillation 
If Instant Craft isn’t checked, then the value of this option will be used to make Crafts, Fermentations and Distillations go this much faster. Note that this doesn’t just change the game speed. 

 Deactivate All Alert Levels & Game Over 
If checked, all systems of Game Over and Alert Level going up are deactivated. Events linked to a specific Alert Level should get deactivated too.

notes.title: The Moonshine’s (alcohol) Family Tree
notes.content:
Hello Moonshiners! Today we have a last #MoonshineMemoirs update for you. Today we gonna show you a bit trivia about some distinctive, peculiar, and odd alcohols, not necessarily found in the game, but to be found in high-proof cultures around the world. As you will see, inspiration lurks everywhere. Because...

Anyone can make moonshine.
Hardly anyone can make good moonshine.

And anything can be a base for moonshine, as long as it then gets distilled - and strong.

But there are strong and distilled drinks that became so traditional, original, culturally important, that they have long shed the name of moonshine, and became something so much more. 
Of course, that includes all that we know so well; whiskies, vodkas, gins, tequilas, rums. And brandies, cognacs, rakijas, grappas. Ouzos and absinthes, and tons of other ‘medicinal’ herb-based spirits. And generally all those things based on grains, sugar, potatoes, pomace/grapes, figs, and other fruits that we know in Europe and North America. Generally - all moonshine based on traditional American and European fruits of the earth either got its own name - or remained a moonshine.

But what about some things more exotic, ingredients less known? What else can moonshine be based on and then grow into something so much bigger, so much more important than just a basic backyard pot still rotgut. Well, for example, we have:

Palm wine
Palm wine is a fine base for strong alcohol - especially since it’s already an alcoholic drink… In Ghana, a strong liquor distilled from it is known as akpeteshie, while in Nigeria - ogogoro.
Of course, palms are spread all around the world, so a similar and traditional distilled brew, lambanog, can be found as far as the Philippines!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/6edb00343f642c210b7c7ec2359b8696dd873d84.jpg
*Drinking palm wine from a calabash

Jujube
Dates are a base for many different types of alcoholic beverages, including different types of rakijas and brandies. Mahia, a Moroccan brandy, can be distilled from it, as well as from figs, and grapes… and jujubes, described in ‘Wild Jujube (Ziziphus lotus) Control in Morocco’, an article from 1995, as a ‘deciduous, thorny shrub that causes complete wheat and other crop loss by preventing harvest operations’. It seems jujube messes up the crops - so the people avenge that by distilling the bastard.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/926ee55597530ca8e283b3abf3a4307fd8208deb.jpg
*Bottle of Mahia Meknesiah, France

Sorghum
Sorghum is a type of plant from the grass family. It’s sometimes grown for food, sometimes for animal fodder - and sometimes for alcohol. Baijiu, a traditional distilled spirit from China, is based on it. And since sorghum, just like palm trees, is spread across quite some distances, in the faraway - from a Chinese perspective - Kenya it’s too a popular source of distilled beverage. When combined with millet and maize, it creates changaa, a very strong spirit (to which, prior to current laws, manufacturers would add jet fuel and battery acid to give it an extra kick… But let’s not consider those a fine basis for alcohol!)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/b64a6a9103858fd94e395d2aca2ce5b1d57b719d.jpg
*A glass and bottle of Jiugui, 酒鬼

Raisin
Brandies, rakija, grappa; so many alcohols are based on grapes and pomace! But what about raisins? Well, being old and wrinkly doesn’t mean a grape lost its spirit - quite literally in case of aragh sagi, an Iranian beverage, known also as Persian vodka. In the end, it is technically a moonshine, since it’s illegal to produce it - but it’s a moonshine so traditional, it's got its own name!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/de4973e7934616dae5b057db586e190468bec067.jpg
*An old picture of Aragh Maykadeh

Ti plant
Last but definitely not least we have okolehao, a distilled beverage from Hawaii, made from the roots of the ti plant. Don't know what a ti plant is? Understandable. Also known as palm lily and cabbage palm, it's more closely related to asparagus than a palm, and it’s been distilled by the fine folks from the exotic islands ever since the distillation technology was brought there by the English. Baked ti root is placed in water, starts fermenting, and gets distilled - and becomes a powerful, powerful drink.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/27d06a456fd4b0fa9df983434bb402e231b80247.jpg
*Hawaiian Ti Plant -- Cordyline fruticosa

It is not like anyone has a chance to be a moonshiner but in Moonshine Inc. you can, for sure, try your hand at this apt craft.

notes.title: The Story, the Legend
notes.content:
Hello again, Moonshiners! In today's #MoonshineMemoirs let's have a look at the story of none other than you - the main character in Moonshine Inc.

It’s not easy to make a name for yourself in the big city. With skyscrapers looming over, people always rushing everywhere, and the ‘hollow sound of silent people walking down the stairway to the subway in the shadows down below’. Kris Kristofferson knew what he was singing about more than too well. 
So how can a simple country boy make a career there? 
He cannot.
But what about a not-so-simple, smart country boy? 
Well, he too will find it challenging. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/b90d71d3101a1554a862f4119108128dc3a1d873.png

And that’s exactly what happened to our main character. He thought he was destined for something more than the simple country life, he tried to escape it, to make a name for himself. And he failed. As simple as that. Not made for the merciless city life he was. And now he has to return to his homeland, with more debts than good memories - and barely any hope for the future.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/d5de085358889b1b7d25313c8ed17c12963910b8.png

But you don’t need hope when you have a family that will stand by your side no matter what. Which wasn’t too obvious to the main hero at first, sure. But one look at his little sister, one shriek - of happiness - from her powerful lungs, and he knew that he was more than welcome back home. And when Elly-Jane suggested she’ll help him learn how to make moonshine, set up a business, and tell gruncle Donald to share his vast knowledge on spirit-making (and to stop grumbling), it became more than apparent that the bad fortune might be turning for the better. As long as the hero was ready to work his ass off to reach his goals.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/d9824a228351e1ccde7a351c40c59ee399fb498b.png

And that’s the basics of the story and the background of the main character. Country boy turned city boy turned country boy again, and proud of it, and glad. Now all he needs to do is build his moonshining empire, outsmart the police, deal with pesky ATF agents, not fall into traps set up by corrupt governors, and… have a little fun while doing all that. ‘cause that’s what being a moonshiner is all about.

notes.title: Red Flag Police alert system
notes.content:
Greetings Moonshiners! 

Let's start the countdown! Only one week left until the premiere of Moonshine Inc.!

Latterly, we've shared some shiny copies with the press, media, influencers, and, in general, with several nice content creators.
Therefore expect a fair few new updates and prolly some videos of Moonshine Inc around the web. 

[hr][/hr]

And as the big launch is quickly approaching, check out the new #MoonshineMemoires!

A spider in the mash. A leaking pot still. A mistake in proofing and suddenly all your clients go blind. There are many obstacles, troubles, and challenges that moonshiners face. But none of them is worse than… being caught by the police.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/4d5f2db248aae7ab9bfdda98658519392c61ffee.png

And the same goes for Moonshine INC. and our original Red Flag Police alert system. 
When delivering moonshine to your clients, most often you have to get it to one of your stashes. You can choose where a given batch goes, you can divide the batches between different stashes. There are always a couple of those on the map for you to choose from.

However, choosing the right stash is not so easy. Each one has its own statistics which depend on how often you use it. First of all, the more you use a given stash, the more popular it becomes. BUT, the popularity of the given stash increases the probability of a police raid. And that’s the exact opposite of what you want. A raid destroys the batch in your stash and lowers its popularity back to zero. 
So, you have to be very careful when you choose where to make your delivery. While dividing a delivery among different destinations might seem like a clever idea, you might want to give a certain stash a pass if it’s become too popular among the people (and thus the police). 

The other thing to worry about is the general Police Alert. This particular statistic is global and is also affected by your dealings and how discreet you are. The bigger the level of the Alert, the bigger the chance of your drivers running into events during the deliveries. There are different types of events, but they often may prove a challenge for you and require making decisions right there on the spot. Dispose of a batch and escape safely? Or maybe risk a police chase but make the delivery? Luckily, some of your employees - whom you can set as drivers for the given delivery - might have Traits that help with that, like better driving and so on. So that’s good. But it’s even better when the police don’t notice you at all. Especially since once, the Police Alert becomes too high… It’s game over, man. Game over.

Fortunately, there are some ways of lowering the Police Alert level. Those too include the road events during the deliveries, so it’s not all that bad. And the other thing? Side-missions. There’s more than just stashes on the map - there are also prominent members of the local community who might want something a little… special. Helping them, being discreet, as well as some luck, are the main ways of keeping yourself safe from that dreaded Johnny Law. And of becoming a proper, world-class moonshiner.

notes.title: BUILDING YOUR BASE
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/58144f0680758ab6314adc31fa653c83cee6024c.png

Your secret HQ is the heart of your operation - worth mentioning, illegal ones!
You’ll be building and upgrading facilities, developing new apparatuses, hosting your employees, and most importantly, it is here that you’ll be making fine moonshine. Please treat it with respect, as your home and workshop in one.

At least, that’s a general idea.

In your base, you'll find a couple of specific buildings. The Employees' Headquarters, for example. Clicking on it opens a menu with the list of your current hired workers, their statistics, statuses, specializations, and so on. It’s essential to keep track of everything happening in your base.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/4e350dcd17b38813dba22400ec61560cd037dd0c.jpg

Then there is The Warehouse. It opens the Inventory where you’ll keep your ingredients, the alcohol waiting to be delivered, and equipment and apparatuses that need to be placed around the base.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/6ce3ae1309dfe258dfc4d903d5de9e7c1b5040a7.jpg
*) one well-equipped warehouse


The area of your base is divided by a grid. That’s where you’ll be putting all the apparatuses when you craft them. You can create all sorts of machinery: fruit presses, grain mills, fermentation tanks and barrels, and finally - distillation stills. And all types of those.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/a55e703d38f3659b9e29b60d88fe0d4bf18e6627.jpg

Given the amount of equipment you’ll be able to craft, you’ll have to organize and arrange everything properly. But that doesn’t mean you can’t give it a bit of... personal touch. Maybe you want all your pre-fermentation equipment next to each other? And distillation on the other side of the base? Or everything together to easily keep an eye on the whole operation? And to possibly make it easier for your employees. Who sometimes have to go quite some distance to get to the river and grab some good, clean mountain water for fermentation and distillation.

In the end, building your base is entirely up to you. Ergonomic and economic, visually pleasing and appeasing - whatever you want. It’s your base, after all! And around it, you’ll build your empire.

notes.title: CRAFTING OVERVIEW
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/636ed21378864d05c51f8489e4bd8c88a6748566.png

Crafting is an essential skill for any moonshiner. After all, you won’t - and can’t! - be buying
your illegal equipment at any ordinary store. Instead, crafty moonshiners have to get different
parts - pots, copper sheets, coils, wooden kegs, and so on - separately and then combine
them to create a perfect spirit-distilling apparatus. Some famous folks have
their own styles and are Appalachian-wide famous for their skills! So why not join their
respectable ranks?

Of course, a distillation pot is just one of the many different types of equipment we need.
Before any distillation can occur, first we need fermentation - and pre-fermentation before
that too. And that’s the first category of crafting. Pre-fermentation lets you create a mash.
A different apparatus will be required depending on the ingredients you want to use for your drink. For example, if you want apple brandy, you need a fruit press for those apples
to make them, well, comply - and thus get mashed. And for grains you need, of course, to
craft a grain mill.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/ef291dde1363406976a5de6176e27d12128587b0.jpg

And that’s just the beginning. Naturally, the pre-fermented mash has to be then fully fermented. For that, you’ll need specific tanks and canisters. There are many different types of those, from small barrels for open fermentation to proper, proper tanks with closed decks.

But the real essence of crafting is in building state-of-art distillation apparatuses. Here you’ll choose their basis, a still, the size of which can range from a traditional basic pot to a nearly industrial metal giant. 

What’s more, you’ll be able to choose the type of fuel used, as well as the type and size of the thumper keg. Thanks to that, you’ll be able to fully customize the very heart and soul of your operation.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/c3b8705b1eeea380688d5470f3d3368c5730eb1e.jpg

The last category of crafting is post-distillation. The apparatuses within this category will
allow you to alter the final taste of your spirit. For example, you’ll be able to age it to fit the
palates of the more exquisite clientele or macerate/redistill it with botanicals to create new,
unusual, and exotic brews, dilute the spirits by adding more water to save, or fortitude it with previously distilled high spirits to reach higher voltage!

And one last thing: crafting is all fine and good, but you can’t do any of it without your
employees. And money. And remembering that equipment needs to be maintained, repaired,
and cleaned... And all that which a proper boss has to supervise to make sure the operation
goes without fail.

[hr][/hr]

notes.title: Distillation Mechanics Overview
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/cd623edc4df63005c599fc0e4af564194c31f256.png

Let's have a look at the complexity of the mechanisms that shape the game.

To start producing alcohol in the game you first have to open the production window. There you’ll be able to choose ingredients that will later become alcohol. Those include many types of fruits and grains, depending on what you’re after. 

If it’s whiskey, go with grains; if it’s brandy, choose some sweet and ripe cherries or grapes, and so on. And if it’s moonshine… well, go with whatever. Moonshine forgives more than other alcohols. But there are many recipes to discover and you can experiment! 

And if you’re not sure what to do, you can follow recipes that you’ll learn during the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/e3be43c8cd4dff3c476f53fc7ebd0b9c0b9a4b8d.jpg
Process of fermentation

When the ingredients are chosen (you can mix a few different ingredients together!), you’ll have to then select the right and preferable type of yeast and apparatuses, such as fermentation tanks and pot stills. You’ll also have to set the temperature of the fermentation which might affect, for example, the amount of mash produced.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/8d22e843a0c3dc9c30e98144fb940e82cf177019.jpg
Process of distillation

Once some time has passed and the fermentation is done, we can move on to distillation. There too we can adjust a few things. Those include the flow of the distillation as well as which parts will be foreshots, heads, hearts, tails, and general waste. While hearts are where quality and taste lie, adjusting other sliders can increase the ethanol level, producing a stronger brew. And for some people, the strength of the drink is much more important than the quality. Remember that the client is always right!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/e4400d94e39e429e4ad0b2b766120917d99209b6.jpg
Process of bottling

The last process is bottling. This is the final moment when you can affect the quality, strength (you can fortify or dilute it), and quantity of your alcohol. You can also set the price… and give your brew a fancy name.

notes.title: How the Magic Happens
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/eceb5fa749b17537b18c58df1d01dc5fc53110e3.png

There are many phases to the moonshing process and sometimes even the smallest mistake can destroy the whole thing.

If we don’t control the gas burner it might explode - or a nosey rat might just bite its way into our barrel of sweet apple mash!

Before distillation can take place, we need to create our mash - the thing that will be later distilled. There are many different types of those, main ones being based on fruit or grains. You can’t make rye whiskey without rye - same as a cherry bounce brandy would be no good without cherries!

Grains - these you have to wet first and keep them for some time in warmth, so that they can sprout.

Fruit - you want to be as ripe as possible. 

When you later add water and yeast the latter’s enzymes cause the whole thing to ferment. Fermented mash is the thing you then distill in the pot still by heating it up and making the mash start to evaporate. The vapors are then liquified again and you get your alcohol. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/3d91682381d46653cfc830dac2cb74e0b1ae02d9.jpg Image courtesy of Wikimedia Commons.

Of course, the process described above is all about the very, very basics - as it’s been aforementioned, true moonshinin’ requires a ton of skill! An experienced moonshiner might, for example, add a thump keg which will cause the liquified vapors to evaporate again (and liquify again too), creating a stronger alcohol. There are even whole column stills made out of chambers that do that as well, one after another! And that’s not all. The alcohol you get might be later aged (and the outcome of this depends on what kind of barrel you use for that!), redistilled with different kinds of botanicals, fortified or diluted…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/e3be43c8cd4dff3c476f53fc7ebd0b9c0b9a4b8d.jpg

And all those things you’ll be able to do in our game!


Mill and press ingredients before making them into a mash; control the temperature of fermentation; even harvest yeast! 

You’ll also learn how to use different types of stills; and how to make your product perfect via all sorts of post-distillation processes. 

And, most of all: you’ll be able to experiment and discover, and create all sorts of different recipes!

notes.title: Risky Whiskey Business - the Fortunes and Misfortunes of Moonshiners
notes.content:
Many wealthy and famous people made their money selling illegal alcohol. Al Capone and other Prohibition-era gangsters come to mind first. But what about ‘the little man’? A simple farmer who makes a ton of cash selling the golden - or crystal clear - liquid fruits of his labor?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/b46e2fd987fa3bc369fe12a10313aed3f1f94590.jpg
*) Well-known mug shot of Al Capone - Photographic File of the Paris Bureau of the New York Times

The most famous moonshiner would be Amos Owens (ca. 1822 – 1906) from North Carolina. He settled down on Cherry Mountain, where he started producing the alcohol he called ‘Cherry Bounce,’ the popularity of which earned him the nickname ‘The Cherry Bounce King.’ And quite understandably so - this combination of whiskey, cherries, and honey was so famous people from all around would come to buy it. Even a big celebration would take place, come cherry harvest season!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/6955b7ae6684377b127d6fa70773c9042934ba50.jpg
*) "The Cherry Bounce King", Amos Owens - North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources

Speaking of the Cherry Bounce... the good ol’ first president, he, too, didn’t stray away from moonshine, made similarly to the famous Owens' hooch. Once the most famous POTUS retired, he started distilling his rye whiskey. Although just a few years prior, he put a giant tax on alcohol - and even squashed (though without bloodshed) the Whiskey Rebellion that followed…

But while Amos Owens’s story is that of success, we have to talk about the misfortunes of the trade too. So let’s talk about Buck O’Hairen (ca. 1837 - ?), another famous and successful moonshiner from North Carolina. After the Civil War, he came to his fortune when many folks from the South moved west to escape possible new age repercussions. But Buck stayed. And started producing moonshine. And a lot of it. In 1873 he was making 60 gallons - 227 liters a day!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/3d7bc3aec4ab048bbe6d1242284523f9db9835e0.jpg
*) Buck O’Hairen’s mugshot — believed to be the only known photo of him - courtesy of whoisbuckohairen

Sadly, in 1874 one of Buck’s stills exploded, destroying everything and causing a massive wildfire. And so his luck and fortune were gone within an instant. In the end, Buck changed his ways and started producing a non-alcoholic drink, called Sunshine, to be drunk in the morning so that it would “fix yer mornin’ right.” But in 1892, Buck suddenly disappeared, and no one knows what happened to one of the most famous and rich moonshiners.

And here we are - two different, two famous, two incredibly rich moonshiners from North Carolina. Two stories prove that moonshining is a lucrative but risky business. In the end, no matter how powerful you are, just a straightforward mistake may cost you… well, everything.

notes.title: Bootlegging and Sports Cars, or the Original Fast and Furious
notes.content:
When we talk about bootleggers, many folks might think about such characters as Al Capone. And it’s true, he was a gangster dealing with, among other things, sales of illegal alcohol. But he wasn’t necessarily out there, where the daredevilish drivers were actually trying to smuggle booze right underneath the police's noses. These true bootleggers were the real American heroes - Smokey and the Bandit style.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/0b19dbd6667fb4f5e1f643f6a751c7699e74adb6.jpg
*) Dumping wine, Chicago, Illinois, 1921, Chicago History Museum

The word ‘bootlegging’ comes from, well - hiding illegal goods in one’s boots to avoid the ever-watchful and always hungry eyes and hands of the law. However, during the times of Prohibition, when alcohol became illegal (and before and after that when alcohol was heavily taxed), the smugglers found a much more effective way of smuggling goods: cars. Fast, fast cars. Thanks to them the bootleggers were capable of travelling vast distances within just a few hours, crossing a state border after a state border. To put it simply: someone had to get alcohol from its source - for example, a tiny farm in the middle of the Appalachian Mountains - to its destination: a fancy speakeasy in New York, where the rich and fabulous were relying on the poor to help them party all through the night.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/975359d38e89f604e1101ad1b7fcec2be51519ed.jpg
*) Moonshine Inc, different set of base's comparison, concept art

Of course, the police could not be expected to stay behind. And so a wild development of car technology began, with the bootleggers customizing their cars and police trying to match that, all while the general progress of the industry was producing more and more powerful machines and technologies (Edmund Fahey, a famous bootlegger, even claimed that some companies created stronger car tires especially for the rum smugglers). The many contraptions used by the smugglers included things straight from a modern action movie: removing all the unnecessary parts of the car so that it’s lighter, changing license plates, and… using the strong moonshine as fuel, should a need arise.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/0b33d2d3a3e23cca59d0afd94aa4d4cd0e99a7f6.jpg
*) Moonshine Inc, choosing the destination

This interest in fast cars and their customization, taking place mostly in the South, led to a whole culture being born around it. A part of it was the idea of the so-called ‘stock car’ - an absolutely normal, factory-line car, adapted for driving in special conditions, such as a race or a demolition derby. And this in turn led to one of the most famous and American competitions: National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing… or NASCAR for short. And, unsurprisingly, some of the first - and most - famous champions included former bootleggers: Carl D. “Lightening” Lloyd Seay, “Rapid” Roy Hall, Junior Johnson, and many, many more…

notes.title: From Zero to Hero, or how the distilling technology evolved
notes.content:
The most famous and historically significant ancestor of the modern still is an alembic. The alchemists used it to create all sorts of distilled liquids for religious rituals or science in general - not really for drinking. The alembic consisted of three different elements. The first one was a still pot with a cap, not dissimilar to the ones used nowadays by the moonshiners.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/215eb6d60698ccb16621123f1680e948e5b6de28.png
*)Moonshine Inc, 3D models set up

The liquid in this pot was heated over a flame. The vapors would stop at the top of the pot and then liquify, going down a unique tube straight to a receiving vessel. The alembic was a straightforward apparatus, but it was based on the exact mechanisms that we use today. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/603a549d7618a497954bb2b0e53c226aa663e406.jpg
*)Moonshine Inc, screenshot - Distillation

As it often turns out to be the case, not much has changed in the distilling technology from the 19th century and later. However, the Industrial Revolution and the modern ever-advancing technological progress do not omit such vital areas as distilling (and general booze-making). For example, an essential invention for distilling was a reflux column. To visualize it, one must imagine a column made out of many different pots (chambers), one stuck on another, with tiny holes. The way it works is similar to a simple pot still. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/e907c1fd082a8fe75cc7107c211d87590e73396f.jpg
*)Moonshine Inc, screenshot - Crafting

First, the alcohol evaporates and then stops at the cap of the pot; but the lid has tiny holes, so it evaporates further, where it stops on another cap; and that one too has holes, and so on, until the vapor reaches the very last cap of the column, where it goes down a pipe into a container (same as in a normal, simple still). This process allows the given brewmaster to create a much stronger, multiply-distilled alcohol.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/94f7e2b9b16e60b8f8df7575e6923374c69666f0.jpg
*)Moonshine Inc – T(a)esting moonshine!

So, we’ve come a long way from a simple alembic to an industrial reflux column. But, of course, that’s not it - there are as many stills as there are moonshiners! The tube where the alcohol liquifies can be a coil (called ‘worm’). A still may have a doubler/thump keg, a clever invention working similarly to the reflux column but being much more minor - basically yet another box next to a still pot, where the liquified alcohol goes only to be heated again. The stills can be made of copper. They can be made of steel. And every moonshiner can add something new! Like hanging a cotton bag with fruits inside the still so that the vapors combine with the fresh taste of the fruit. Or using wood chips to accelerate the aging of your whiskey! Or building a giant, so-called ‘submarine still’ and just really going for it...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/4868579bee1d7144adb9fc92d7cafb0725c45697.jpg
*)Moonshine Inc, screenshot – Bottling!

Stay with us for more #MoonshineMemoires and meanwhile please or let us know your opinions on Steam or Discord!

notes.title: *Ping* Wake up, 'Leggers! We have a moonshine to brew!
notes.content:
We have been silent for some time – sorry for that, but it is because we have been working hard to prepare a first playable demo version of our beloved Moonshine Inc. So yeah, finally, on February 21st, 2022, you will be able to put your hands on Moonshine Inc, as we opted in for the next STEAM Demo festival. 

Meanwhile, to keep you entertained and on track with our development, we will keep on sharing some exciting content about bootlegging, moonshining, and of course on game mechanics and game-related content.

Next year will be an exciting time for our studio. We have planned a very ambitious road-to-market plan including closed beta, open beta, demo festival, events activity, so follow us here on STEAM, join our Discord, or keep in touch to be updated. 

To start, let's take a look at the history of alcohol distilling to shine a light on moonshining!

There isn't an exact, universal description telling us precisely what the so-called moonshine - white lightning - fire water - aqua vitae (Latin for 'water of life') - bathtub gin (yup) - good ol' mountain dew - is. However, it's generally understood as a strong, distilled drink. The name 'moonshine' is typically used for whiskey. Still, moonshiners don't mind venturing into the vodka, brandy, or other whatever-the-client-demands territories - as long as it's distilled and illegal, it's moonshine. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/4d01ad27d07315687006f8c0f9296eea8862317c.jpg
*) A tax collector is tarred and feathered by anti-tax frontiersmen during the Whiskey Rebellion.     The Granger Collection, BEW

Still, the Whiskey Rebellion of 1791 is one of the most critical events in moonshining history. It was then that President George Washington decided to tax alcohol. Since most distillers were poor farmers, the people had no other choice but rebel. Then again, nothing much happened. When Washington sent 13,000 militiamen at the very climax, most people just went home, not wanting to fight an entire army. 

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/71ced4aa30daa19daf29d5c91e4f689dd1dca6ce.jpg
⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀*) Whiskey tax, public domain

And so the tax remained, and so the people started hiding their illegal stills better, and in the end, it all didn't matter since the tax was repealed a couple of years later. Then it returned, disappeared, changed, and so on, and so on. And now we have today, when alcohol is taxed and when some people hide in the middle of the woods to make it illegally - the same as those two hundred years ago. Still, man does not live on whiskey alone.

There's evidence that in 1200 BCE in Mesopotamia, people already generally knew about distillation. But it was a simple process, and the outcome was not drinkable. Of course, the wine-loving Greeks and Romans had better technology, but it wasn't until the 12-13 centuries when people (all around the globe; Arabic countries, Europe, China…) finally realized how to make - and drink - the proper, modern(ish) water of life. Then people realized that you could distill (or ferment and then distill) almost anything - and the fun began.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35074365/f6b8b05fc1d190b470752094201e0a587b636ed3.jpg
*) An Egyptian funerary model of a bakery and brewery. ( CC BY-SA 2.5 )

Fast forward to today, and, putting all the sugar, grape, potato, cereal, and plum based alcohols aside (because there's just too many of those to count!), we have the exotic raisin-based zarbali from Afghanistan, Ghanian akpeteshie (distilled from palm wine), Tunisian-Jewish boukha (figs), nocino (walnuts, Italy), okolehao (Hawaii, ti plant), and rice-based soju (Korea), shōchū (Japan) and Laotian lao-lao. In Kenya, there's kumi kumi, in Cameroon mfofo. Chacha in Georgia, kachasu in Malawi. 

And then there's arak, araqi, arrack, raki, rakia, rakija, raksi, each different, spread from the Levant to Tibet, and each moonshine - as long as they're strong, illegal, and homemade.

Stay with us to learn more about moonshining as next we will focus on "From Zero to Hero, or How Distilling Technology Evolved".

Mooshine Inc. - this isometric economic simulator with RPG elements in which you will develop your character, obtain multiple companions, and build your moonshining empire from the ground - gets not only new title, but also significant changes in gameplay and story.
